Market Intelligence Briefing
subheadings: 🇺🇸 United States Mixed on hold / hawkish-leaning transition
🇪🇺 European Union Bullish steady ECB / growth upside
🇨🇳 China Bearish easing bias / weak domestic demand
🇯🇵 Japan Bullish pro-growth vote / tolerant yen
🇵🇱 Poland Bullish late easing / strong growth
🔬 US–Asia Semis — SOXX / ASML / TSMC Bullish
🧮 Earnings Pattern — What the Market Pays For
Guidance over beats: the market pays for AI that earns and sells AI that costs
🔍 Underowned Themes — Attention and Exposure Gaps
India after the US tariff reset
US natural gas after the storm-spike collapse
Bitcoin breaks its floor: a liquidity event in a policy vacuum
Dollar bounce, parallel rates drift, and credit's software problem
🔮 Anticipatory Positioning — Markets Pricing In Future Events
Alphabet and Amazon: the capex tolerance test
$GOOGL — AI winner into Wednesday's print Bullish
$AMD — a soft guide breaks the second-source story Bearish
Gold dip-buyers / GLD — the retail hedge
BitMine & Strategy / BMNR, MSTR — leveraged crypto treasuries
SpaceX proxies — the private-market access trade
body: Wednesday, February 04 2026 — Macro · Sectors · Flows · Crypto
Information cutoff: 2026-02-04 00:00 UTC. Market figures use completed observations before this date.

Macro Stance: Growth is running hotter than sentiment: the January ISM manufacturing PMI printed 52.6% PR Newswire [Feb 02] while consumer confidence fell to its lowest since 2014 Bloomberg.com [Jan 27]. The BLS delayed the January jobs report because of the partial shutdown Bloomberg.com [Feb 02], and traders read Kevin Warsh as a more hawkish pick for chair Bloomberg.com [Jan 30]. Firm factories, weak households and a hawkish-leaning transition argue for a Fed on hold, not the cuts the White House wants.

Rates & Curve: The 2Y closed at 3.57% and the 10Y at 4.28%, a 10Y−2Y spread of 71 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03). Both rose 11 bps over 20 observations, so the spread change was 0 bps: a bear-steepening label on what is in substance a parallel sell-off, with the curve moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03). Equities slipped from near-record levels: the S&P 500 fell 0.8% to 6,917.81 and the VIX jumped 10.2% to 18.00 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

New / Most Important: The market's problem is AI disruption, not the economy: Wall Street ended sharply down on AI fears Reuters [Feb 03] as new AI tools wiped $300 billion off software and data stocks WSJ [Feb 03], and the damage spread to Blackstone, alternative managers and BDCs as software woes infected private credit Barron's [Feb 03]. On trade, the deal cutting US tariffs on India to 18% Reuters [Feb 02] removes one overhang.

Playbook ✓: Keep equity beta near benchmark but rotate into energy and AI-capex industrials (XLE, XLI), funded from seat-based software, and hold 2Y–5Y Treasuries rather than the long end while the 30Y sits at 4.90% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03). Add duration only if the delayed payrolls print shows a clear labour downturn or the 10Y falls back through its 20-observation-ago 4.17%; turn defensive if the VIX holds above 18.00 while HYG makes new lows.

Macro Stance: The euro area heads into the ECB meeting from strength: Q4 GDP unexpectedly grew 0.3% Financial Times [Jan 30] and banks drove European stocks to a record high Reuters [Feb 02]. A central bank that can sit on hold while growth surprises upward is the best setup for European cyclicals and lenders.

Credit & Inflation: The caution flag is credit: the ECB's survey shows euro-zone banks tightening access to business credit Reuters [Feb 03], and the German 30-year yield climbed to its highest since 2011 Bloomberg.com [Feb 03] — a term-premium warning for long-duration assets. The STOXX 600 closed at 617.93, up 2.1% over 20 sessions, and EUR/USD slipped 0.4% to 1.1799 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

New / Most Important: AI disruption crossed the Atlantic: RELX and Wolters Kluwer plunged on AI competition fears WSJ [Feb 03]. The DAX is down 0.5% over 20 sessions while the FTSE 100 is up 1.9% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): bank- and resource-heavy indices are beating those with software and industrial-tech weight.

Playbook ✓: Overweight euro-area banks and industrial cyclicals; underweight information-services and data publishers WSJ [Feb 03] until AI pricing pressure is visible in guidance. Keep long-end Bund exposure light while the 30-year sits at post-2011 highs Bloomberg.com [Feb 03]. Change the call if the next PMIs or lending survey show tighter credit Reuters [Feb 03] biting into activity.

Macro Stance: China is a two-speed economy: exporters and high-tech manufacturers carry growth while household and property demand keep sliding. The first fiscal revenue drop since 2020, driven by the property slump and weak consumption Reuters [Jan 30], shows how narrow the base has become. We stay bearish on the domestic-demand complex and selective on exporters and policy beneficiaries.

PMIs & Activity: The January official manufacturing PMI dropped to 49.3 Reuters [Jan 30], while the private survey showed factory activity growing at the fastest pace since October and beating the official reading CNBC [Feb 01]. The gap is the story: the private gauge leans to export-oriented and private firms, the official one to large domestic and state-linked producers. Until the official index recovers, the domestic economy is not turning.

Credit Impulse: The latest credit read (December) was weak: 2025 new bank loans were the lowest in seven years, with Reuters noting policy support is needed Reuters [Jan 15]. Easing has lowered funding costs but not created borrowers, so we read the credit impulse as still negative. A January print with rising household loans would be the first confirmation of a turn; the feed carries none yet.

Property: Property remains the drag: sales declines accelerated in a 'bleak start' to 2026 for the sector South China Morning Post [Feb 02]. Beijing's measures so far support prices and developer funding rather than demand, which is why developer equities rally on policy headlines and then fade. Until new-home sales stabilise, property-linked banks and building materials are funding sources, not holdings.

Fiscal, Policy & Trade: Fiscal firepower is being rationed — the revenue drop Reuters [Jan 30] limits room for a large consumption push — while trade frictions keep shifting: Washington's $12 billion minerals stockpile is designed to counter China Reuters [Feb 02]. That stockpile, set against Xi's call for the renminbi to attain reserve-currency status Financial Times [Feb 01], shows both sides building strategic buffers rather than de-escalating, which favours China's upstream and state champions over consumer exposure.

Markets & Flows: The Shanghai Composite rose 1.3% to 4,067.74 but is down 0.4% over 20 sessions, and the Hang Seng gained 0.2% to 26,834.77 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). KWEB fell 1.9% to 34.42 and is down 5.6% over 20 sessions as Chinese tech stocks slid to the brink of a bear market on tax concerns Bloomberg.com [Feb 03]. ASHR closed at 33.24, down 1.3% over 20 sessions, FXI is down 3.0%, and USD/CNY eased to 6.9463, a 0.6% yuan gain over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

New / Most Important: The currency is the new driver: Xi has called for the renminbi to attain global reserve-currency status Financial Times [Feb 01], and the yuan's 0.6% gain against the dollar over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) is consistent with managed appreciation. A firmer yuan supports A-share inflows and importers but squeezes exporters' margins — the very sector carrying growth. Separately, the tax scare that hit Chinese tech Bloomberg.com [Feb 03] shows platform regulation risk has not gone away.

Playbook ✓: Prefer onshore A-shares (ASHR) and yuan exposure over Hong Kong-listed internet names (KWEB) until the tax concern is resolved; avoid developers and property-linked lenders. Add to China cyclicals only on a January credit print with rising household loans Reuters [Jan 15] or an official PMI back above 50. ⚠ Divergence: the private manufacturing PMI's fastest growth since October CNBC [Feb 01] says activity is firmer than the official 49.3 suggests Reuters [Jan 30].

Macro Stance: Japan is Asia's cleanest pro-growth trade: polls show PM Takaichi's party poised for a landslide Reuters [Feb 01], which would give the government room for fiscal support and a tolerant stance on the yen. USD/JPY at 155.44 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) shows currency markets already lean that way.

Activity & Currency: Japanese stocks jumped more than 3% to a record high CNBC [Feb 02]: the Nikkei 225 rose 3.9% to 54,720.66 and is up 5.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). USD/JPY rose 0.7% over five sessions but is down 0.8% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), so the yen has stabilised rather than collapsed — a better backdrop for domestic earners than for exporters.

Playbook ✓: Own Japanese equities with the currency hedged, favouring banks and domestic cyclicals over exporters already priced for a weak yen. Keep a small long-yen option as the hedge against an earlier BOJ hike or intervention. Cut exposure if the expected landslide Reuters [Feb 01] fails to materialise or JGB yields spike.

Macro Stance: Australia reversed course with a rate hike and markets are betting on more Reuters [Feb 03]: the RBA raised the cash rate 25bps to 3.85% Reuters [Feb 02]. A central bank re-tightening straight after an easing cycle is telling markets it no longer treats inflation as transitory, and domestic demand will carry the cost.

Demand & Financing: Mortgage holders absorb a hike first, while bank margins widen as loans reprice. AUD/USD closed at 0.6956, up 3.6% over 20 sessions, and the ASX 200 rose 0.9% to 8,857.10 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): the currency, not equities, is the cleaner expression of a hawkish RBA.

Playbook ✓: Underweight rate-sensitive domestic cyclicals and REITs; prefer the major banks, which gain from loan repricing, and keep a long-AUD bias while markets price further hikes Reuters [Feb 03]. Reverse if monthly CPI rolls over or unemployment jumps, which would end the hiking talk.

Monetary & Activity: Poland pairs strong growth with low inflation: GDP grew 3.6% in 2025 xyz.pl [Jan 31], and December inflation came in below the midpoint of the NBP target (Polish: 'Inflacja w grudniu 2025 stanęła poniżej środka celu NBP') Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK [Jan 15]. The MPC decision is pending, and Credit Agricole economists expect an NBP rate cut ('przewidują obniżkę stóp NBP') Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK [Feb 02]. With inflation inside the band a cut is affordable; a hold would keep real rates high and the zloty firm.

FX & Markets: EUR/PLN closed at 4.2200, up just 0.2% over 20 sessions, and USD/PLN at 3.5768 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). The WIG20TR ETF rose 2.1% to 68.38 and EPOL 1.8% to 38.35, led by KGHM up 8.9% to 340.00, Pekao up 4.8% and PKO BP up 3.2% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Companies: KGHM is the market's metals lever: it lost 15% at the open during the metals rout Money.pl [Feb 02] and is still up 14.7% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). CD Projekt fell 3.5% to 250.70 and is down 5.7% over five sessions as Google's playable-world AI model weighs on video-game stocks Reuters [Jan 30], while Allegro is down 7.1% and Dino 7.5% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): gaming and consumer names lag the bank- and metals-led rally.

Security & New Development: Defence is becoming a domestic capital-markets theme: Poland awarded the Kongsberg-PGZ consortium a $1.65B counter-drone system contract The Defense Post [Feb 02], a multi-year order stream for state-owned PGZ and its domestic suppliers that keeps security spending, not just consumption, as a growth driver.

Playbook ✓: Stay overweight Poland via EPOL and the WIG20TR ETF with banks (PKO BP, Pekao) and PZU as the core: a hold protects margins, and a cut Miesięcznik Finansowy BANK [Feb 02] would read as growth-supportive. Trade KGHM tactically around copper, keep Allegro and Dino underweight, and fade EUR/PLN spikes above 4.2200 if the MPC holds. ⚠ Divergence: index strength leans on KGHM, whose 8.9% jump came days after a 15% opening loss Money.pl [Feb 02] — a narrower, more commodity-driven rally than the growth story implies.

Narrative: Consensus still treats AI as a tailwind for all of tech; the market now prices it as a disruptor of software economics, with new AI tools wiping $300 billion off software and data stocks WSJ [Feb 03]. XLK fell 2.2% in the prior session and is down 1.8% over 20 sessions, with Microsoft down 14.4% over five sessions and Oracle down 19.7% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: Microsoft lost $357 billion in market value as the stock plunged the most since 2020 after its results CNBC [Jan 29], the clearest case of AI spending being punished. Palantir beat estimates and the stock rallied CNBC [Feb 03], rising 6.9% to 157.88 in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

EPS Upside Watch: Storage and memory hardware carry the cleanest estimate momentum: TrendForce sees chip prices up 90-95% quarter on quarter in Q1 Reuters [Feb 02], straight into memory margins and against device makers' costs. Apple is up 4.3% over five sessions to 269.48 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), with component costs the swing factor for its margin guide.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Palantir rallied on the same day software was dumped CNBC [Feb 03]: the market is separating platforms that sell AI outcomes from seat-based applications that AI can replace. Short per-seat SaaS baskets rather than XLK outright.

Narrative: Communication services is a two-megacap sector with a split tape: Meta jumped 10% on a stronger revenue forecast CNBC [Jan 28], while Netflix is down 12.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). XLC fell 1.6% in the prior session and is flat over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: Meta's stronger revenue forecast CNBC [Jan 28] shows the market will pay for AI spend once it shows up in ad revenue. Legacy media is getting the opposite treatment: Disney is down 5.8% over five sessions to 104.22 and 8.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): investors are not paying for content owners without a visible AI revenue line.

EPS Upside Watch: Alphabet is set up to surprise, with results Wednesday Investopedia [Feb 02] and traders ramping long bets toward a $350 share price TradingView [Feb 03]. GOOGL closed at 339.71, up 7.3% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Alphabet is now a disruptor inside its own sector: its prompt-to-playable-world AI model knocked video-game stocks Reuters [Jan 30]. Owning the platform while avoiding the content and services layers it can automate is the trade the market is rewarding.

Narrative: Financials are splitting between balance-sheet banks and asset-light models exposed to AI: Blackstone, alternative managers and BDCs dived as software woes infected private credit Barron's [Feb 03], while money-centre banks held up. XLF fell 0.9% and is down 4.6% over 20 sessions, but JPMorgan rose 2.2% and Bank of America 0.8% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: PayPal sank on a CEO exit and a disappointing 2026 profit forecast Reuters [Feb 03], and Goldman Sachs slipped 0.8% to 938.99 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): payments and capital-markets franchises are being de-rated while deposit-funded lenders hold up.

EPS Upside Watch: Mortgage originators have operating leverage to mortgage rates holding near three-year lows MarketWatch [Jan 30], and banks earn more on a 71 bps 10Y−2Y spread that is moderately steep, approaching the long-run average (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03). Net interest income, not trading, is where 2026 estimates can rise.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Banks drove European stocks to a record high Reuters [Feb 02] while US alternative managers were sold Barron's [Feb 03]: the market pays for regulated balance sheets and sells the private-credit model that was supposed to replace them. Long JPM and BAC against an alternative-manager basket captures the split.

Narrative: Energy is the market's hedge of choice: XLE rose 3.2% in the prior session and 10.2% over 20 sessions, with Exxon up 14.7% and Brent up 9.0% to $67.33 over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Oil climbed 2% after the US shot down an Iranian drone Reuters [Feb 03], so geopolitics, not demand, is setting the marginal price.

Reported: Exxon and Chevron are producing record amounts of oil, but lower prices led to lower earnings MarketWatch [Jan 30]; Chevron is still up 8.7% over 20 sessions to 178.04 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), so the market is paying for volume resilience.

EPS Upside Watch: Gulf Coast refiners: the US is soon to issue a general licence for oil production in Venezuela Reuters [Feb 03], adding the heavy barrels complex US refiners are built to run — a crack-spread tailwind more dependable than the crude price itself.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The price risk is two-sided: oil settled down over 4% on a single day of US-Iran de-escalation Reuters [Feb 02]. With XLE up 10.2% over 20 sessions on what is largely a risk premium (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), a diplomatic breakthrough would hit energy equities first.

Narrative: Industrials are the cleanest beneficiary of AI capex without the software-disruption risk: XLI is up 5.7% over 20 sessions and Caterpillar 14.1%, including 10.0% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). The January ISM at 52.6% PR Newswire [Feb 02] says the broad factory cycle is turning up as well.

Reported: Caterpillar rose on revenue and earnings beats driven by demand for power-generation equipment Yahoo Finance [Jan 29], and GE Vernova's Q4 gas-turbine orders surged 74% Utility Dive [Jan 30]. GE closed at 309.93, up 4.2% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

EPS Upside Watch: Power equipment remains supply-constrained: turbine orders up 74% Utility Dive [Jan 30] are backlog that converts into revenue over several years, so revisions for gensets, turbines and switchgear should keep rising. Boeing, down 4.7% over five sessions to 233.15 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), is the laggard to watch as aerospace rejoins the cycle.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The policy backlash is starting: Washington state is debating making data centres pay full power costs Axios [Feb 03]. If hyperscalers carry more of the grid bill, data-centre timelines stretch — a risk for an AI-power trade that consensus treats as one-way.

Narrative: Discretionary is where the K-shaped economy bites: consumer confidence fell to its lowest since 2014 Bloomberg.com [Jan 27]. XLY fell 0.8% in the prior session and is up only 0.6% over 20 sessions, with Tesla down 6.6% and Nike 5.6% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: Chipotle forecast weak annual sales and margin pressure as consumers cut discretionary spending Reuters [Feb 03], while Home Depot, up 10.8% over 20 sessions to 381.10 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), is bid on housing hopes rather than current demand.

EPS Upside Watch: Amazon reports Thursday, with options pricing a large post-earnings move Investopedia [Feb 03]; AWS growth against capex is the swing factor. AMZN is down 2.5% over five sessions to 238.62 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), so expectations into the print are lower than for Alphabet.

⚡ Breaking Convention: PepsiCo plans to cut snack prices even as its drink sales improve CNBC [Feb 03]: consumer pushback is strong enough to force price cuts on a staples giant, so discretionary pricing power is weaker still. Value formats and off-price retail win; brands that rely on price increases lose.

Narrative: Staples have become the momentum defensive: XLP rose 1.6% in the prior session and is up 11.0% over 20 sessions, with Walmart up 9.2% over five sessions and Costco 11.7% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Walmart became the first retailer to reach a $1 trillion market value Reuters [Feb 03].

Reported: PepsiCo's drink sales are improving, but it is planning to cut snack prices CNBC [Feb 03] — volume recovery bought with margin. The market's preference is clear: scale retailers that turn price cuts into traffic (Walmart, Costco) over brand owners that must fund them.

EPS Upside Watch: Walmart's scale Reuters [Feb 03] lets it convert price investment into share gains, the main source of estimate upgrades in a stretched consumer economy. Costco at 977.92 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) offers the same model with membership-fee leverage.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Staples are now crowded: an 11.0% 20-session gain for XLP (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) is a momentum move, not a valuation-led defensive rotation, and price cuts in packaged snacks CNBC [Feb 03] cap the earnings upside. Own the retailers, not the packaged-food basket.

Narrative: Healthcare is cheapening on pricing risk: XLV fell 1.0% in the prior session and is down 0.6% over 20 sessions, with UnitedHealth down 16.9% over 20 sessions and Lilly down 3.9% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Novo Nordisk's forecast of a steep 2026 sales drop WSJ [Feb 03] set the tone for the obesity complex.

Reported: Merck topped quarterly estimates but posted modest 2026 guidance as generic competition looms CNBC [Feb 03] — the sector pattern of beats with cautious guides. In a market that pays for guidance, big pharma stays range-bound until pipelines replace patent-expiry revenue.

EPS Upside Watch: Lilly carries the operational upside: its CEO says Medicare coverage of obesity drugs could 'change the game' for its pill launch CNBC [Jan 30]. Volume from broader coverage can offset price cuts in a way Novo's guide does not reflect.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Novo's warning WSJ [Feb 03] dragged Lilly lower in sympathy, but a lower price per patient with expanding coverage is a share-shift story, not a demand collapse. The contrarian trade is long Lilly against Novo, not short the obesity theme.

Narrative: Materials are being re-rated as strategic assets: XLB is up 8.8% over 20 sessions and Freeport-McMoRan 18.9%, with copper up 4.5% to $6.06/lb in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Washington's $12 billion minerals stockpile Reuters [Feb 02] and China's plan to expand strategic copper inventories Bloomberg.com [Feb 03] put state buyers under the metals.

Reported: Gold posted its biggest daily gain since 2008 Reuters [Feb 03], closing at $4,935, up 6.1%, while Freeport rose 6.4% and Newmont 3.8% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Miners are trading as leveraged metal proxies into their own reports.

EPS Upside Watch: Copper producers have the clearest estimate upside: copper is up 2.3% over 20 sessions even after the metals rout (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), and it is the AI data-centre and grid-capex metal. Producers that can supply the US stockpile Reuters [Feb 02] gain a price floor that spot exposure lacks.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Precious metals have become a volatility asset: silver jumped 8.2% in the prior session but is down 21.3% over five sessions, and GLD fell 4.6% over five sessions before its 6.4% rebound (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Treat gold and silver miners as beta, not as portfolio hedges.

Narrative: Real estate sits between falling mortgage rates and a sticky long end: mortgage rates are holding near three-year lows MarketWatch [Jan 30], but the 10Y is up 11 bps over 20 observations to 4.28%, and XLRE slipped 0.4% in the prior session, up just 0.9% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03; US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: No bellwether REIT result in the feed window moved the group; price action is set by rates. With the 10Y up 11 bps and the 30Y up 5 bps over 20 observations (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03), long-lease REITs get no help from duration.

EPS Upside Watch: Data-centre and powered-land landlords: the $3 trillion AI data-centre build-out has become all-consuming for debt markets Bloomberg.com [Feb 02], which favours REITs with cheap capital, secured power and pre-leasing over developers that need fresh debt.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Mortgage rates near three-year lows MarketWatch [Jan 30] have not produced a housing-led REIT rally because affordability, not rates alone, is binding; residential landlords and builders need volume, and the feed shows no sign of it yet. Prefer data-centre and healthcare landlords over residential.

Narrative: Barron's calls American Electric Power the safer AI trade Barron's [Feb 03], and the tape agreed in a risk-off session: XLU rose 1.5% and NextEra 2.9%, with NextEra up 9.2% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Merchant generators are the opposite story — Constellation is down 24.4% and Vistra 6.1% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: NextEra is betting on gas as its data-centre pipeline holds steady at about 15 GW Utility Dive [Jan 29]. Contracted demand with regulated returns is what the market is paying for, while merchant exposure to power-price politics is being sold.

EPS Upside Watch: Regulated utilities with rate-base growth from data-centre interconnections, such as AEP and NextEra Barron's [Feb 03], have the most visible EPS growth. Merchant IPPs (CEG, VST) have more upside to power prices but carry cost-allocation risk.

⚡ Breaking Convention: The political backlash is building: Washington state's debate on making data centres pay full power costs Axios [Feb 03] is a template for cost allocation elsewhere. The merchant IPPs' 20-session slump says the market fears price caps more than it values scarcity.

Narrative: European autos remain a structural underweight: the SXAP tracker is down 4.4% over 20 sessions, with BMW down 5.8%, Stellantis 12.3% and Renault 12.7%, Renault falling 4.2% in the prior session alone (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). One in 10 cars sold in Europe is now made by a Chinese brand Automotive News [Jan 30].

Reported: No major European carmaker reported in the feed window; the group traded on competition and tariffs. Volkswagen preference shares slipped 0.5% to 102.25 and are down only 0.8% over 20 sessions, holding up better than peers (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

EPS Upside Watch: German premium brands have a tariff tailwind: India will slash tariffs on high-end EU cars from 110% to 30% The Economic Times [Jan 28]. Mercedes held up best, up 2.8% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), and is the cleanest way to own that upside.

⚡ Breaking Convention: Chinese brands' one-in-10 share Automotive News [Jan 30] means price competition hits Europe's volume segment first, while premium makers face it mainly in China. The better trade is long Mercedes and BMW against Renault and Stellantis rather than a blanket sector short.

Narrative: Semis are in a memory-led supercycle: TrendForce sees chip prices surging 90-95% in Q1 from the previous quarter Reuters [Feb 02]. SOXX is up 8.7% over 20 sessions despite a 2.0% drop in the prior session, led by Micron up 34.4%, Intel 25.1% and ASML 13.7% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Reported: AMD predicted weaker first-quarter sales and the shares plunged on Nvidia comparisons Reuters [Feb 03]. Broadcom is down 6.7% over 20 sessions and Nvidia 4.1% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): the market is rotating from compute to memory and equipment.

EPS Upside Watch: Memory makers and equipment suppliers: price increases of that scale Reuters [Feb 02] flow largely to gross margin, and ASML at 1,395.88 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) benefits as memory makers add capacity. TSM, up 4.2% over 20 sessions to 335.75, has lagged and offers cheaper leading-edge exposure (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

⚡ Breaking Convention: Customers are pushing back on the AI leader: OpenAI is reportedly unsatisfied with some Nvidia chips and looking for alternatives Reuters [Feb 03]. That could help custom silicon and second-source GPUs over time, but for now the spend is flowing to memory, not to Nvidia's challengers.

Rewarded: Meta jumped 10% on a stronger revenue forecast CNBC [Jan 28], Palantir rallied after beating estimates CNBC [Feb 03], and Caterpillar rose on beats driven by power-generation demand Yahoo Finance [Jan 29]. Over 20 sessions Caterpillar is up 14.1% and Micron 34.4% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): owners of AI bottlenecks are being paid.

Punished: Microsoft plunged the most since 2020, losing $357 billion of market value CNBC [Jan 29]; PayPal sank on a CEO exit and a weak 2026 profit forecast Reuters [Feb 03]; AMD fell as its first-quarter forecast disappointed Reuters [Feb 03]; and Novo's steep 2026 sales-drop forecast WSJ [Feb 03] hit the obesity complex.

Pattern: Beats are table stakes; the reaction is set by the guide and by who carries the AI cost. Investors rewarded Meta's revenue forecast CNBC [Jan 28] and punished Microsoft's results CNBC [Jan 29] because Meta showed AI revenue while Microsoft showed AI spending. Companies selling into the bottleneck (memory, power equipment) are rewarded; those whose product AI can replicate are sold even on beats.

Attention into EPS: Alphabet reports Wednesday Investopedia [Feb 02] and Amazon Thursday Investopedia [Feb 03], with Eli Lilly also on the week's slate CNBC [Jan 30]. The hyperscaler question is capex against cloud revenue: whichever shows more cloud growth per dollar of capex will be treated like Meta, the other like Microsoft.

Playbook: Into prints, own the bottleneck (memory, power equipment, grid) and avoid paying up for capex-heavy names without revenue acceleration. Sell beats with soft guides on the first rally; buy guide-raisers on the first pullback. Change the call if Alphabet and Amazon both raise capex and are rewarded — that would mean the market is paying for AI spend again.

Attention Gap: The US cut tariffs on India to 18% while India agreed to end Russian oil purchases Reuters [Feb 02], removing the largest single overhang on Indian exporters. The deal turns India from a tariff casualty into a beneficiary of supply-chain diversification away from China — a re-rating that rarely completes in one session.

Exposure & Risk: Express through broad India ETFs (INDA, EPI) tilted to financials and industrials rather than IT services, which dived 6% as Anthropic's AI plug-ins shook the staffing-intensive sector Reuters [Feb 03]. Risks: the deal's terms still need detail, and India's IT exporters face the same AI-disruption repricing as US software, which caps index-level upside.

Attention Gap: Henry Hub gas fell 52.4% over five sessions to $3.31/MMBtu and is down 6.0% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), a collapse that reads as a weather unwind rather than a demand break. The structural bid is intact: Qatar Energy's CEO says AI power needs may turn the LNG glut into a gap by 2030 Reuters [Feb 02], and NextEra is leaning on gas for its data-centre pipeline Utility Dive [Jan 29].

Exposure & Risk: Use gas-weighted producers (EQT) or LNG exporters (Cheniere) rather than front-month futures, whose roll costs and weather sensitivity dominate returns. Risks: a mild end to winter could pin prices near current levels, and power-price politics may cap how much gas-fired generators can pass through.

Market Context: Bitcoin's prior completed daily close was $75,633.55, down 3.9% on the day, 10.6% over five sessions and 22.0% over 20 sessions; ether closed at $2,227.56, down 33.6% over 20 sessions, and solana at $97.56, down 33.5% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). IBIT is down 19.0% over 20 sessions, Coinbase 29.5% and Strategy 19.1% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Bitcoin briefly broke below $73,000, its lowest since November 2024 CNBC [Feb 03].

New / Most Important: The selloff is a liquidity event layered on a policy vacuum. Strategy's shares slid after bitcoin briefly dipped below the firm's key breakeven level CNBC [Feb 02], turning the largest corporate holder from a source of demand into a source of stress. A Fed chair pick that traders read as hawkish Bloomberg.com [Jan 30] removes the easy-money narrative, and the dollar's 1.3% five-session bounce (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) tightened the liquidity crypto runs on.

Playbook: Bearish. Do not catch the knife until bitcoin reclaims the $79,000 rebound level CoinDesk [Feb 02]; a break of the $73,000 intraday low CNBC [Feb 03] opens room to the next round-number supports. Prefer spot exposure via IBIT over leveraged proxies (MSTR, BitMine) and hedge with puts rather than outright shorts given squeeze risk. Turn constructive on stabilising ETF flows or a regulatory breakthrough on stablecoins.

Rates & Dollar: DXY closed at 97.44, up 1.3% over five sessions after the Warsh nomination Bloomberg.com [Jan 30] but down 0.8% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). The 10Y at 4.28% and 30Y at 4.90% leave the curve moderately steep, approaching the long-run average, with the 30Y−10Y spread at 62 bps (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03). TLT fell 1.2% over five sessions, LQD 0.6% and HYG 0.6% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Credit Check: Primary markets are wide open — global bond sales reached $1 trillion at their fastest pace ever Bloomberg.com [Feb 02] — but stress is migrating to private credit, where alternative managers and BDCs dived on software exposure Barron's [Feb 03]. HYG is down only 0.2% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), so public high yield has not priced the private-credit repricing; that gap is the risk.

Portfolio Implication: Keep IG over HY and public over private credit; avoid BDCs and alternative managers until software-loan marks are visible. Keep duration in the 2Y–5Y sector while the 30Y holds at 4.90% (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-03), and fund international equity overweights from US software. Reverse if HYG breaks to new lows with the VIX above 18.00, which would signal private-credit stress leaking into public markets.

What Is Priced: Iran and the US are set to hold nuclear talks on Friday Reuters [Feb 03], after oil climbed 2% when the US shot down an Iranian drone Reuters [Feb 03]. Brent closed at $67.33 and WTI at $63.21, up 9.0% and 8.4% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) — a risk premium rather than a lost barrel.

Conditional Expression: If talks progress, expect a repeat of the day oil settled down over 4% on de-escalation Reuters [Feb 02]: own refiners and airlines and fade upstream. If talks collapse or military action follows, own XLE and Brent call spreads; the equity hedge is cheaper than crude upside.

Risk: Venezuelan supply is set to rise as the US prepares a production licence Reuters [Feb 03], so de-escalation could erase Brent's 20-session gain quickly. Conversely, a strike would threaten Gulf supply routes and make today's premium look small.

What Is Priced: Alphabet reports Wednesday Investopedia [Feb 02] and Amazon Thursday Investopedia [Feb 03]. GOOGL is up 7.3% over 20 sessions while AMZN slipped 2.5% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03): the market prices Alphabet as an AI winner and Amazon as a capex-risk story.

Conditional Expression: If both raise capex with accelerating cloud revenue, buy the AI-infrastructure supply chain (memory, power equipment) and the reporters on dips. If capex rises without cloud acceleration, expect a Microsoft-style reaction CNBC [Jan 29] and rotate further into staples and energy.

Risk: The AI build-out is already consuming debt markets Bloomberg.com [Feb 02], so a capex raise funded with debt could be punished even with strong cloud growth. A hawkish read of the Fed transition with higher real yields would compress the multiples these prints need.

Catalyst & Thesis: Results land Wednesday Investopedia [Feb 02]. Thesis: Alphabet monetises AI through search, cloud and models and is disrupting adjacent industries such as gaming Reuters [Jan 30] rather than being disrupted — the profile the market rewarded at Meta.

Price Hurdle & Risk: GOOGL closed at 339.71, down 1.2% in the prior session and up 7.3% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03). Positioning is crowded, with traders ramping long bets toward $350 TradingView [Feb 03]; express via call spreads and step aside if capex guidance rises without cloud acceleration.

Catalyst & Thesis: AMD predicted weaker first-quarter sales and the shares plunged on Nvidia comparisons Reuters [Feb 03]. Thesis: in a market paying only for raised guidance, a second-source GPU vendor with a soft quarter loses its premium while memory and foundry capture the scarcity.

Price Hurdle & Risk: AMD closed at 242.11 before the report, down 1.7% on the day but up 9.5% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03) — gains that are exposed. Risk: OpenAI is looking for alternatives to some Nvidia chips Reuters [Feb 03], and a large order would revive the share-gain thesis; cover on such news.

Observed Attention: Retail traders aren't giving up on SLV even after silver's plunge CNBC [Feb 02]. SLV fell 24.2% over five sessions before rebounding 6.2% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Motivation & Bias: Dip-buying anchored on the prior peak and a debasement narrative around the Fed transition; the bias is anchoring — a lower price feels like value even though the volatility regime has changed.

Instrument & Risk: SLV options carry extreme implied volatility after the crash; size small, use defined-risk spreads, and treat the rebound as a range trade inside the five-session drawdown rather than the start of a new leg.

Observed Attention: Retail buyers flocked to buy gold despite the sell-off Bloomberg.com [Feb 02]; GLD rebounded 6.4% to 454.29 in the prior session after a 4.6% five-session drop (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Motivation & Bias: Gold is the retail hedge against a politicised Fed and a weaker dollar; the bias is narrative persistence — buyers treat the drop as a discount rather than a sign the trade was crowded.

Instrument & Risk: GLD is a cleaner vehicle than miners or leveraged ETFs, and gold is still up 10.9% over 20 sessions at $4,935 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03), so dip-buyers are not yet underwater on a one-month view. Risk: another forced-liquidation wave if the dollar extends its bounce.

Observed Attention: Stocktwits flags BitMine in focus after ether's sharp selloff Stocktwits [Feb 02], and MSTR closed at 133.26, down 17.5% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-03).

Motivation & Bias: Retail treats crypto-treasury stocks as leveraged, 'discounted' crypto exposure; the biases are authority (following famous bulls) and sunk-cost anchoring as unrealised losses mount.

Instrument & Risk: These equities embed balance-sheet leverage: bitcoin dipped below Strategy's breakeven CNBC [Feb 02], which can collapse the premium to holdings. Prefer IBIT for spot exposure; if holding MSTR or BMNR, hedge with puts.

Observed Attention: A rare SpaceX bet has turned a $1.1 billion fund into a retail magnet Bloomberg.com [Feb 01]: retail is buying access to a private company through whatever listed wrapper holds it, and the wrapper's premium is the trade.
Motivation & Bias: Access scarcity: retail cannot buy SpaceX directly, so it pays up for proxies and closed-end vehicles; the bias is scarcity-driven fear of missing out on a private-market winner.
Instrument & Risk: Proxies can trade at large premiums to underlying value that collapse on IPO-timing news; size as an option, not a core holding, and do not add after spikes.
